pages.title: Where should I start?
pages.detail: Follow the payment example, inspect the Elixir-to-Lean connection, or open Case Lab. Choose a reading path that fits what you want to learn.
pages.limit: Catalog counts describe available claims, not a fresh proof run.

pages.title: Why does a timeout keep the hold?
pages.detail: Start with the empty account and follow each event. Compare the before and after state, then open the selected moment in Case Lab.
pages.limit: This runs the local ledger model. It does not contact a payment processor.

pages.title: Which part of the system does this work?
pages.detail: Choose a component or hold state to see its role and source. Follow a request from the ledger to the runtime and modeled processor.
pages.limit: Real processor behavior and storage durability need separate evidence.

pages.title: What behavior does the policy require?
pages.detail: Choose a payment requirement, compare the expected behavior with a possible mistake, then read its related claims.
pages.limit: The complete claim determines which inputs and outputs it covers.

pages.title: Which claim covers the behavior I care about?
pages.detail: Search for an event, example or claim name. Each profile gives a concrete situation, the required behavior and source links.
pages.limit: Reading families organize the catalog; they are not proof dependencies or checker results.

pages.title: What does a claim promise?
pages.detail: Follow exact fit from the payment requirement to requires and expects. Read which inputs the claim covers and which output it demands.
pages.limit: Reading the statement is separate from checking a proof of it.

pages.title: What does the evidence establish?
pages.detail: Check what produced a result, which source it covers and what it assumes. Use these distinctions when reading reports in Case Lab.
pages.limit: A proof about a model does not establish real storage durability or processor compliance.

pages.title: Where is the source?
pages.detail: Choose the question you are investigating and follow its file or claim link. The directory also includes the named mutation and policy examples.
pages.limit: An example description is not a freshly executed check.

pages.title: What does this word mean here?
pages.detail: Search a word or alias, read its repository example and follow the related guide. These entries also appear in contextual help.
pages.limit: Read the original statement when exact conditions matter.

pages.title: How do these pieces fit together?
pages.detail: Follow the reading map from policy through implementation, claims and proof evidence. Open the stage that answers your question.
pages.limit: This is a reading order, not a logical dependency graph.

pages.title: Which claim is meant to catch this mistake?
pages.detail: Choose a named source mutation. Read its changed behavior, concrete input and target claim, then inspect the linked source.
pages.limit: This page explains committed examples; it does not run a mutation campaign.

pages.title: What does Lynx contribute?
pages.detail: Read the Elixir source and law, available generated Lean, and the checked-in theorem. Each pane identifies where its text came from.
pages.limit: Generated source can be unavailable. Checked-in proof text alone is not current verification evidence.

pages.title: Does this changed claim still cover the requirement?
pages.detail: Read the policy and proposed change, choose your conclusion, then reveal the worked explanation. Optional notes help connect your reasoning.
pages.limit: These are two practice studies. Proposed claim changes are not checked by Lean here.

pages.title: What does this case show?
pages.detail: Try an event, inspect the code result and test a proposed output against the claim. Open Inspector for the condition tree and proof source.
pages.limit: A case check covers the selected input and output, not every possible execution.

pages.title: What does this case show?
pages.detail: Try an event, inspect the code result and test a proposed output against the claim. Open Inspector for the condition tree and proof source.
pages.limit: A case check covers the selected input and output, not every possible execution.

lab.claim.short: Open a claim and a prepared case for it.
lab.claim.detail: The claim determines which input conditions and output promise you are inspecting. Read its title before trying an event.
lab.claim.limit: Changing claims opens a different case. Save temporary events first if you want to keep them.

lab.compare_sources.short: Choose two saved source versions to compare.
lab.compare_sources.detail: Select a staged original and proposal, then run the same case against both. The opening example change is an illustration.
lab.compare_sources.limit: A difference is a case to review. Matching results for the tried cases do not prove the versions equivalent.

lab.snapshots.short: Select the original and proposed source versions.
lab.snapshots.detail: These are trusted local snapshots prepared outside the browser. The app checks that their files still match the recorded version.
lab.snapshots.limit: Selecting a snapshot does not run its code or verify its proofs.

lab.run_versions.short: Evaluate this case with both selected source versions.
lab.run_versions.detail: Each version runs separately. Compare which inputs its claim covers, which outputs it allows, and what its code returns.
lab.run_versions.limit: This comparison covers the tried case, not every possible execution.

lab.open_events.short: Apply another event to the selected state.
lab.open_events.detail: Try dispatch, timeout, retry, cancellation or a processor result. The event stays temporary until you save it to the timeline.

lab.save_to_timeline.short: Keep the events you have tried in this review session.
lab.save_to_timeline.detail: Save when you want to return to this sequence later. Reset and reload discard events you have not saved.
lab.save_to_timeline.limit: Saving events does not record a review decision or verify a claim.

lab.reset.short: Discard temporary changes and return to the saved timeline.
lab.reset.detail: Use this to start again from the recorded case. Previously saved steps remain available.

lab.timeline.short: Inspect the account and event at this point in the history.
lab.timeline.detail: New events run from the selected step. Moving through the timeline does not erase the other steps or forked paths.

lab.amount.detail: A new request needs enough available amount and a free hold slot. Changing the amount previews a case; save it to keep the event.
lab.amount.limit: An input outside the selected claim may still have a policy requirement.

lab.boundary.short: Try a request just below, at, or above the available amount.
lab.boundary.detail: The buttons use the remaining capacity in the selected state. An exact fit must be admitted when its key is new and a slot is free.
lab.boundary.limit: A larger request can be outside the exact-fit claim. That does not mean the claim proved its rejection.

lab.propose.short: Change the answer you want to test against the claim.
lab.propose.detail: Edit the result, held amount, entries or requested effects. The code returned the other output; this one is your proposal.
lab.propose.limit: A proposal the claim accepts still needs to be compared with the payment policy.

lab.proposed_result.short: Choose the result your proposed output should report.
lab.proposed_result.detail: Try a different result while keeping the rest of the output visible. The claim check updates for this proposal.
lab.proposed_result.limit: This changes a proposed answer, not the implementation.

lab.proposed_amount.short: Change the held-amount counter in the proposed output.
lab.proposed_amount.detail: The editor keeps your value even if it disagrees with the entries. Use Recalculate totals when you want counters derived from those entries.
lab.proposed_amount.limit: A changed counter is an illustration; the code did not return it.

lab.status.short: Try another status for this entry in the proposed output.
lab.status.detail: Watch whether the claim accepts the changed status and whether the account remains consistent. Other output fields keep their current values.
lab.status.limit: Changing a local status does not change a real processor authorization.

lab.preset.short: Check a small set of prepared alternative outputs.
lab.preset.detail: This looks for an output worth inspecting against the selected claim. Read the result and conditions after a proposal is found.
lab.preset.limit: It does not change the source or search every possible output.

lab.mutate.term: Change part of a proposed output
lab.mutate.short: Apply the named change to the proposed output.
lab.mutate.detail: Remove effects, zero counters or change an identity to examine a specific mistake. Other values remain available for inspection.
lab.mutate.limit: This is a proposed output, not an executed source mutation.

lab.restore.short: Copy the code result into the proposed output again.
lab.restore.detail: Use this to undo your output edits while keeping the selected input and timeline.

lab.recalculate.short: Set the counters from the holds in the edited state.
lab.recalculate.detail: The editor otherwise keeps the counters you entered, so you can examine inconsistent states deliberately.
lab.recalculate.limit: Recalculating counters alone does not establish that the whole state or proposed behavior is valid.

lab.advanced.short: Edit the full proposed state, result and effects.
lab.advanced.detail: Use structured fields or JSON when the quick controls cannot express your example. Invalid input clears the previous check.
lab.advanced.limit: This editor accepts bounded example data; it does not execute pasted code.

lab.add_entry.short: Add a hold record to the state you are editing.
lab.add_entry.detail: Set its request ID, amount and status. Counters remain unchanged until you edit or recalculate them.

lab.add_effect.short: Add a proposed request to cancel an authorization.
lab.add_effect.detail: Choose the key whose authorization the proposed output should ask the processor to void.
lab.add_effect.limit: An effect requests outside work; it does not mean that work has completed.

lab.clear_effects.short: Remove requested outside work from the proposed output.
lab.clear_effects.detail: This helps examine whether the claim requires the correct authorization or void request.
lab.clear_effects.limit: The proposed state stays as you edited it.

lab.branch.short: Create a second timeline path starting from your proposed output.
lab.branch.detail: One path keeps the code result. The other uses your proposal as the starting state for later events.
lab.branch.limit: The proposal must be a valid state before it can be continued.

lab.run_paths.short: Apply the same next event to both timeline paths.
lab.run_paths.detail: Compare the continuation from the code result with the continuation from your proposed output. Both use the same implementation.
lab.run_paths.limit: These paths are different from comparing two source versions.

lab.event_fields.short: Choose the event and the request it concerns.
lab.event_fields.detail: The request ID identifies the hold. An amount is used for a new request; other events use the fields relevant to that event.
lab.event_fields.limit: Processor events here act on the local model.

lab.starting.short: Build a different account state for a new case.
lab.starting.detail: Edit its limits, counters and entries, then choose Run from this state. This creates a separate review session.

lab.conditions.short: See why the claim accepts or rejects this case.
lab.conditions.detail: Inspect the input conditions and required result with their observed values. Expand an expression to read its parts.
lab.conditions.limit: The values explain the selected case; they are not a proof of every input.

lab.proof.short: Read the Lean statement and the proof supplied for it.
lab.proof.detail: Start with the theorem header, then open the proof text if you want to follow the argument.
lab.proof.limit: Source text is separate from a current verification report.

lab.assumptions.short: Inspect the processor behavior the model relies on.
lab.assumptions.detail: Try a supported assumption change and compare the local ledger with the modeled processor.
lab.assumptions.limit: A modeled assumption is not evidence that a real processor honors it.

lab.artifacts.short: Read the generated source and available verification reports.
lab.artifacts.detail: Check the source version, claim scope and status attached to each report before using it as evidence.
lab.artifacts.limit: Missing or stale files cannot establish current acceptance.

lab.notes.short: Read the judgments and questions saved for this case.
lab.notes.detail: Notes record what a reviewer found. They are separate from the temporary events in an unsaved experiment.
lab.notes.limit: A review note does not change a proof result or the editorial status of an explanation.

lab.review.short: Save your judgment about the selected claim and case.
lab.review.detail: Flag a concern, leave an open question or mark the case reviewed. Add context when it helps explain the decision.
lab.review.limit: This does not save temporary events or establish formal acceptance.

lab.note_context.short: Explain what you noticed in this case.
lab.note_context.detail: Connect the policy, claim and concrete input or output. Your notes stay separate from assistant questions.

lab.evidence_choice.short: Choose the stored finding your review decision concerns.
lab.evidence_choice.detail: The selected evidence identifies the source versions and case being reviewed. Read its status before recording a conclusion.

lab.save_case.short: Keep this input and proposed output as a review case.
lab.save_case.detail: Save temporary events to the timeline first. The stored case retains its source and selected claim.

lab.basis.short: Choose which output supplies the values in the condition view.
lab.basis.detail: Code returned uses the computed result. Proposed output uses the answer you are testing against the claim.

lab.binding.short: Inspect one set of values substituted into the claim.
lab.binding.detail: Some claims consider several entries or combinations. This selection changes the values shown in the condition tree.
lab.binding.limit: One displayed combination does not replace the aggregate case result.

lab.clause.short: Follow this part of the claim into its explanation and source.
lab.clause.detail: Read the values and expression together. A reviewed source link may also identify a related Lean passage.
lab.clause.limit: Source correspondence does not show a saved Lean goal state.

lab.helper.short: Open the definition or supporting statement used here.
lab.helper.detail: Follow it when the name alone does not explain what the condition or proof requires.

lab.source.short: Open the source passage or report named by this control.
lab.source.detail: Source links refer to the files recorded for this claim. If the source has changed, reopen the claim before relying on an older reading.

lab.coupled.short: Compare local ledger knowledge with the modeled processor.
lab.coupled.detail: Follow issuance, delivery and local observation as separate events. A missing local reply can leave a live remote authorization.
lab.coupled.limit: The model does not contact a payment processor.

lens.mode.term: Choose how to read the exercise
lens.mode.short: Choose whether to see the explanation before making a judgment.
lens.mode.detail: Review first asks for your conclusion before showing the worked explanation. Explore freely shows it while you try the example.
lens.mode.limit: Changing modes clears the current practice answer.

lens.classification.short: Choose the conclusion you think this example supports.
lens.classification.detail: Ask whether the claim leaves out a required input, accepts a forbidden output or rejects an allowed output. Choose unsure when evidence is missing.
lens.classification.limit: The answer stays in this practice page; it is not a saved review decision.

lens.confirm.term: Keep my answer and show the explanation
lens.confirm.short: Compare your selected conclusion with the worked explanation.
lens.confirm.detail: The reasoning fields are optional. You can choose that the evidence is insufficient and still read the explanation.

lens.change.short: Try a different input or proposed claim change.
lens.change.detail: Read what changed, then compare its coverage and required output with the original claim. A new example clears your current answer.
lens.change.limit: These are modeled claim changes, not edits to source files.

assistant.send.short: Send your question with the displayed case and source to Codex.
assistant.send.detail: Inspect Shares case + source or Context before sending. The configured provider is Codex; your private review notes are excluded.
assistant.send.limit: The response is a generated explanation. Check proof results in the evidence panels.

assistant.context.short: Read exactly which question, case and source would be sent.
assistant.context.detail: Opening this preview sends nothing. Submit the question only after the displayed context is the one you intend to share.

assistant.history.short: Read a locally saved question and answer.
assistant.history.detail: Reopening history sends no request. A follow-up uses that historical case unless you choose Ask using current case.

assistant.followup.short: Write another question about this saved conversation and case.
assistant.followup.detail: The follow-up keeps the historical case. Inspect its context before sending or choose Ask using current case to switch.

assistant.clear.short: Delete saved local questions and answers after confirmation.
assistant.clear.detail: This removes question history, not review notes or saved case timelines. Deletion is unavailable while a question is running.

lab.view.short: Choose the case overview or the detailed Inspector.
lab.view.detail: Guided keeps the requirement, input, outputs and result together. Inspector opens the conditions and proof source.
lab.view.limit: Switching views keeps the case and unsaved edits.

learn.story.short: Show the account at the selected point in the story.
learn.story.detail: Start with the empty account, then follow a request, dispatch, timeout and second request. The displayed results come from the local ledger model.
learn.story.limit: These controls do not contact a payment processor.

learn.open_moment.term: Open this moment in Case Lab
learn.open_moment.short: Save this story prefix as a case and open its selected moment.
learn.open_moment.detail: Case Lab opens the same account, events and latest result shown here. You can inspect the claim or continue with another event.
learn.open_moment.limit: The new case is a local review session.

learn.retry.short: Try to load the walkthrough from the current source again.
learn.retry.detail: Use this after resolving the displayed source or execution problem. An unavailable result is not replaced with a made-up state.

learn.mutation.short: Read the source change, witness and target claim for this mutation.
learn.mutation.detail: Each example describes one committed source fault. Compare its wrong behavior with the requirement and follow the source links.
learn.mutation.limit: Selecting an example does not execute its patch or run a mutation campaign.

lab.fencing.short: Change whether the modeled processor keeps a void final.
lab.fencing.detail: Compare the ledger with a processor that can revive an authorization after cancellation. The local entry alone cannot enforce remote behavior.
lab.fencing.limit: This changes a model assumption, not a real processor.

assistant.current.term: Start a question about the current case
assistant.current.short: Write a new question using the case currently open in the Lab.
assistant.current.detail: This replaces a historical follow-up context with the current case. Opening the composer sends nothing.

assistant.history_scope.short: Choose whether to show this case’s questions or all local questions.
assistant.history_scope.detail: The selection changes the local history list. Reading an answer does not send another request.

lens.again.short: Clear your practice answer and read the example again.
lens.again.detail: The classification and optional reasoning fields return to their starting state. Saved Lab review notes are separate.

lab.effect_type.short: Choose the outside work your proposed output should request.
lab.effect_type.detail: Authorize asks the processor for a hold; void asks it to cancel one. The key and amount identify the request.
lab.effect_type.limit: This edits a proposed effect. It does not contact a payment processor.

exemptions.reason: Clearly named links state their destination; relevant source and mode links receive authored help where needed.
A descriptive summary names the content it reveals. Conditions, proofs and unclear technical disclosures receive extra help.
Close, copy, previous, next and clear-filter actions state their immediate result.
Ordinary search and optional reasoning fields have visible labels; consequential editor fields receive authored help.

action_exemptions.cancel: The visible Cancel action names the operation to stop; no extra hover help is needed.
action_exemptions.cancel_hunt: Stop search directly names the running preset search.
action_exemptions.close: Close dismisses the current answer panel.
action_exemptions.close_helper: Close dismisses the current source helper.
action_exemptions.close_source: Close source dismisses the source passage.
action_exemptions.close_tools: Done editing closes the editor without creating a new action.
action_exemptions.component: Selecting a named component reveals its authored explanation beside the selector.
action_exemptions.guarantee: Selecting a named requirement reveals its authored explanation beside the selector.
action_exemptions.pipeline: Selecting a reading stage reveals its explanation beside the selector.
action_exemptions.status: Selecting a named status reveals its meaning beside the selector.
action_exemptions.history_page: Previous and Next move through the local history list.
action_exemptions.keep: The cancellation button explicitly keeps question history.
action_exemptions.open: The labeled answer preview opens an existing answer without a provider call.
